title: Malerkotla's Pathan Khwaja Khijar And the death of his two brothers

blocks.text: Dohra:

The messenger Singhs who had been sent to Punjab by Banda Singh, They were asked to return to Banda Singh's camp very soon. (The Majhail Singhs), were asked to converge from Ropar side, While Banda Singh's own forces would make a move towards Sirhind. (1)
lines: The messenger Singhs who had been sent to Punjab by Banda Singh,
They were asked to return to Banda Singh's camp very soon.
(The Majhail Singhs), were asked to converge from Ropar side,
While Banda Singh's own forces would make a move towards Sirhind.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

The Majhail Singhs moved their camp after receiving Banda Singh's message, And very soon reached the Ropar pass as instructed by Banda Singh. When Wazir Khan received the information about Majhail Singhs' arrival at Ropar, He sent Pathan forces of Malerkotla to checkmate their further advance. (2)
lines: The Majhail Singhs moved their camp after receiving Banda Singh's message,
And very soon reached the Ropar pass as instructed by Banda Singh.
When Wazir Khan received the information about Majhail Singhs' arrival at Ropar,
He sent Pathan forces of Malerkotla to checkmate their further advance.

blocks.text: There were four generals in the army of Malerkotla Pathans, Who were the brothers of the late pathan general Nahar Khan of Malerkotla. While Khwaja Khijar and Sher Mohammad Khan were his real brothers, The other two Pathan generals were Nahar Khan's stepbrothers. (3)
lines: There were four generals in the army of Malerkotla Pathans,
Who were the brothers of the late pathan general Nahar Khan of Malerkotla.
While Khwaja Khijar and Sher Mohammad Khan were his real brothers,
The other two Pathan generals were Nahar Khan's stepbrothers.

blocks.text: As this Pathan Army, led by these four generals, attacked the Singhs, The Singhs also took positions to face the brunt of Pathan forces' attack. A fierce encounter took place between the Pathans and the Singhs, As the Pathan forces came too close to the entrenched Singhs. (4)
lines: As this Pathan Army, led by these four generals, attacked the Singhs,
The Singhs also took positions to face the brunt of Pathan forces' attack.
A fierce encounter took place between the Pathans and the Singhs,
As the Pathan forces came too close to the entrenched Singhs.

blocks.text: The brave Majhail Singhs, instead of running from the field, Preferred to come out of their trenches and confront the attacking Pathans. Since it was both an ideological war as well as a war against the Guru's foes, The Singhs were highly motivated to settle scores with the Mughals. (5)
lines: The brave Majhail Singhs, instead of running from the field,
Preferred to come out of their trenches and confront the attacking Pathans.
Since it was both an ideological war as well as a war against the Guru's foes,
The Singhs were highly motivated to settle scores with the Mughals.

blocks.text: Kundliya Chhand:

As the Pathans attacked the Singh with the firing from canons, guns and medium canons, The Singhs took cover in the dug up trenches without deserting the field. Not a single Singh deserted the field during this fierce encounter,

Which compelled the Muslim Pathans to retreat in the face of Singhs resistance. Since too many causalities among them enraged the Khalsa Singhs, Their vigorous offensive uprooted the Pathans abandoning their horses and canons. (6)
lines: Which compelled the Muslim Pathans to retreat in the face of Singhs resistance.
Since too many causalities among them enraged the Khalsa Singhs,
Their vigorous offensive uprooted the Pathans abandoning their horses and canons.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Being informed of this set back, Khawaja Khijar took over the Pathan command, Which made the Singhs beat a retreat for the time being. Then the Khalsa commanders reviewed the whole war situation, And realised that they could not survive through direct confrontation. (7)
lines: Being informed of this set back,
Khawaja Khijar took over the Pathan command,
Which made the Singhs beat a retreat for the time being.
Then the Khalsa commanders reviewed the whole war situation,
And realised that they could not survive through direct confrontation.

blocks.text: So Singhs retreated into their trenches for a longer period, As if they were relaxing in their cantonments during peace time. The Pathan forces used their utmost might to dislodge the Singhs, But the Singhs kept on lying low in their dug up trenches. (8)
lines: So Singhs retreated into their trenches for a longer period,
As if they were relaxing in their cantonments during peace time.
The Pathan forces used their utmost might to dislodge the Singhs,
But the Singhs kept on lying low in their dug up trenches.

blocks.text: The Singhs kept lying low (in their trenches), Waiting for the darkness of night to fall. The Mughals wished for the day to be prolonged, So that they could slaughter all the Singhs. (9)
lines: The Singhs kept lying low (in their trenches),
Waiting for the darkness of night to fall.
The Mughals wished for the day to be prolonged,
So that they could slaughter all the Singhs.

blocks.text: Dohra:

As the sun was going to set and the sunlight going to fade soon, The Muslims felt that even a siege at night would fail to dislodge the Singhs, Even though, the Singhs seemed to have run short of ammunition, And hunger and thirst must have exhausted their energy. (10)
lines: As the sun was going to set and the sunlight going to fade soon,
The Muslims felt that even a siege at night would fail to dislodge the Singhs,
Even though, the Singhs seemed to have run short of ammunition,
And hunger and thirst must have exhausted their energy.

blocks.text: So the Malerkotla Pathan, after reviewing the whole situation, decided, That they should make another attempt to defeat the Singhs, This time Khawaja Khijar led the attack whom the Guru had called coward, Who launched a quick charge at the entrenched Khalsa Singhs. (11)
lines: So the Malerkotla Pathan, after reviewing the whole situation, decided,
That they should make another attempt to defeat the Singhs,
This time Khawaja Khijar led the attack whom the Guru had called coward,
Who launched a quick charge at the entrenched Khalsa Singhs.

blocks.text: Whatever few odd bullets were left in the muskets of the Singhs, They fired those stray bullets at the advancing Pathan warriors. One of these stray bullets hit Khwaja Khijar right into his skull, And he dropped down dead instantly on the ground. (12)
lines: Whatever few odd bullets were left in the muskets of the Singhs,
They fired those stray bullets at the advancing Pathan warriors.
One of these stray bullets hit Khwaja Khijar right into his skull,
And he dropped down dead instantly on the ground.

blocks.text: So died Khwaja Khijar whom the Guru had nick named Khawaja the coward, Who was the most formidable and fleshy among the Pathans. (13)
lines: So died Khwaja Khijar whom the Guru had nick named Khawaja the coward,
Who was the most formidable and fleshy among the Pathans.

blocks.text: The two of his brothers, who came forward to pick up his dead body, They also lost their lives during this vain attempt. As Sher Mohammad Khan came forward after hearing of their death, He also made a fast retreat after getting badly wounded. (14)
lines: The two of his brothers, who came forward to pick up his dead body,
They also lost their lives during this vain attempt.
As Sher Mohammad Khan came forward after hearing of their death,
He also made a fast retreat after getting badly wounded.

blocks.text: Jhoolna
Chhand:

Nawab Sher Mohammad was the sole survivor from this battle, It was he who had protested against Guru's Sahibzadas' murder. It was he who had termed the Sahibzadas' as innocent milk-sucking babes, When Wazir Khan had passed a decree to murder the Sahibzadas. The Guru had spoken the prophetic words after hearing of the Nawab's noble gesture, That Sher Mohammad had saved his generations with his timely protest. (15)
lines: Nawab Sher Mohammad was the sole survivor from this battle,
It was he who had protested against Guru's Sahibzadas' murder.
It was he who had termed the Sahibzadas' as innocent milk-sucking babes,
When Wazir Khan had passed a decree to murder the Sahibzadas.
The Guru had spoken the prophetic words after hearing of the Nawab's noble gesture,
That Sher Mohammad had saved his generations with his timely protest.

blocks.text: Dohra:

After picking up the dead bodies of their three Pathan commanders, The Pathan forces beat a hasty retreat towards Malerkotla. As these three commanders were being burried in their graves, Wazir Khan, the Nawab of Sirhind, felt devastated at the turn of events. (16)
lines: After picking up the dead bodies of their three Pathan commanders,
The Pathan forces beat a hasty retreat towards Malerkotla.
As these three commanders were being burried in their graves,
Wazir Khan, the Nawab of Sirhind, felt devastated at the turn of events.
